propositions: The transition command has two semantically distinct force flags with inconsistent spellings: --force (bypasses start-work gate on open→in_progress) and --force-close (bypasses completion gate on →closed), whereas claim uses --force consistently for both scenarios.

Collapsing transition's two force flags into a single --force[=<reason>] that dispatches by target status preserves existing behavior: on open→in_progress it bypasses start-work, on →closed it bypasses completion, and bare --force on close supplies (no reason given) as the reason.

The hand-rolled _parse_flags loop silently skips unknown tokens, so removing --force-close without explicit rejection would make stale invocations with that flag silently bypass the gate they meant to override; explicit rejection with CommandError is required.

Scripts and documentation that emit or reference the retired --force-close spelling must be migrated in the same change as the CLI rename to prevent runtime failures and ensure the tree-wide grep is genuinely clean post-merge.

Concurrent changes landing after the plan review can introduce new emitters of the retired flag spelling, necessitating a regression test that feeds generated argv to the real parser rather than string-matching, to catch any future rename failures.
